timelineEvents.title: Multiple-language versions and transnational sound-film production
timelineEvents.label: Transnational sound film
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Before 1933, Kaper and Jurmann were already working within the multiple-language version system that linked Babelsberg, Joinville, Vienna, and other European production centres.
timelineEvents.longDescription: The practice of producing parallel language versions was one of the key industrial conditions of early sound cinema. It allowed music to move more easily than dialogue across national markets, even when lyrics, singers, and performance contexts changed. Kaper and Jurmann’s work in this system gave their songs and professional skills a transnational character before their forced departure from Germany.
